title: S5 - does a finer rubric buy resolution or just flatten the distribution
doc_ref: docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/score - 'Use as many levels as you can describe distinctly, up to 10'
note: Eight messages written as a frustration ladder, scored against rubrics of 2, 5 and 10 levels. The ten-level rubric is deliberately at the edge of what can be described distinctly, which is exactly the condition the docs warn about. Two things separate a useful rubric from a wasteful one: whether the ranking improves, and whether confidence survives. A rubric that ranks no better and reports less confidence is strictly worse. Result: the two-level rubric saturates - six of eight states land at 0.99 or 1.00, so it cannot rank at all (rho 0.55). Five and ten levels rank identically well (rho 0.976 each, both disagreeing with the author only on the two adjacent middle rungs), but mean confidence falls from 0.85 to 0.82 and input tokens rise. Ten levels bought no resolution over five.
